Israeli officials believe that it's only a matter of time until the resumption of strikes against Iran, according to a report by Saudi state-owned news outlet Al Hadath on Thursday.
The official told the outlet that the Israeli intelligence has detected an attempt by Iran to revive and activate its nuclear program in anticipation of a strike, following reports in Israel about the regime transferring its remaining nuclear project to Jabal al-Fas, near the Natanz nuclear facility.
The report also cited the official saying that Israel is "defensively and offensively prepared for the possibility of renewed war on Iran and on other fronts as well, at any time."
"We will move to strike nuclear facilities and any site belonging to them again if Tehran crosses any of the red lines, whether with or without the participation of the US," the official added.
The official also warned that the current economic sanctions taken against Iranian-linked entities are generating pressure in Tehran, causing internal division and domestic pressure. "These factors could push it [the Iranian regime] toward military responses in the region, including against Israel."
He then insisted that the only way to have a non-nuclear Iran is through a regime change in the country.
Elections don't constitute a decisive variable against Iran
The official also revealed that the elections in Israel, which will be held on October 27, aren't a factor that could influence the decision-making about striking Iran.
He also said that the current sanctions by the Trump administration are having better effects than expected, with current estimates suggesting that a regime collapse could happen sooner than anticipated.
Finally, the official warned Al Hadath that Israel doesn't see much value in the current negotiations between Americans and Iranians, despite the continuation of contacts and mediations, due to Tehran’s procrastination and its bets on political developments in the United States and Israel that could stop an attack from happening.
Iran, US meet on sidelines of UNGA
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, the first such contacts since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed in July.
"Steve and Jared had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran, merely mediators. Let's see what happens with that," US President Donald Trump said. "They've been mediated for a while, but I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal. It's what we're hearing from everybody."
The Al Hadath report mentioned that no agreement was reached during this meeting, as disagreements continued over several issues, most notably the Strait of Hormuz, in addition to the lack of trust between them.

UN rights chief says civilians are bearing the brunt of fighting in Yemen
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:34:25 UTC
00:34:25 KST

Civilians are being hardest hit by surging violence in Yemen between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Iran-backed Houthis, the UN human rights chief said on Thursday.
The latest fighting marks a sharp escalation in Yemen's civil war, which had largely been frozen since a 2022 truce.
Violence has flared along old front lines in recent weeks, including around Taiz as the Houthis swept south along the Red Sea coast, prompting a humanitarian crisis with over 130,000 people displaced and some fleeing to Africa across the Red Sea.
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said his office has documented the killing of 32 civilians, including 15 children and 3 women, since August in fighting, including drone and missile strikes.
"Civilians are now bearing the brunt of this latest upsurge in fighting," Turk said in a statement, without giving a breakdown of who was responsible for the casualties.
A total of 125 people were documented by his office as killed or wounded in the latest flare-up in the conflict. Both sides allege that hundreds have been killed in fighting over the past weeks, without providing details.
The statement said the UN human rights office had documented three attacks by Ansar Allah, the formal name for the Houthi terrorists, on sites for internally displaced people since August.
It was not immediately clear if the UN toll included any deaths or injuries from those incidents.
Houthis deny UN allegations
Houthi spokesperson Mohammed Abdulsalam said the UN human rights office was no longer impartial, accusing it of ignoring what he described as Saudi bombardment in Yemen that had targeted public facilities.
He cited what he said was the targeting of inmates at a correctional facility in al-Hazm in al-Jawf province, as well as homes and schools in several areas. He said the UN allegations were false and unsupported by evidence.
More than 70 UN staff are being detained by Houthis in Yemen, some of whom have been held for many years. Turk called for their release and urged all the warring parties to protect civilians.
Saudi officials have repeatedly said the country's forces do not target civilians in Yemen. Saudi Arabia's diplomatic mission to the UN in Geneva did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump-Xi meeting outside UNGA spotlight tests world body's clout - analysis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:34:03 UTC
00:34:03 KST

While world leaders gather at the United Nations for their annual diplomatic ritual, the two biggest power brokers in global politics will sit down in a different venue on Thursday: the White House.
US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will meet for the second time this year, hoping to keep the world's most consequential bilateral relationship steady as both leaders grapple with a host of domestic and global issues.
The split-screen moment highlights an existential question for the UN: does the world body, established after the calamity of two world wars, still matter?
While UN delegates discuss "multilateralism" and hold panels on the world's conflicts, Trump and Xi – what the US president calls the "G2" – will talk AI, trade, and defense.
"It's pretty notable that Xi Jinping is coming to Washington in the same week as the General Assembly, but does not feel bothered to come up to New York," said Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group.
"I think a lot of people will say, 'Where is the real center of decision-making?'"
Xi rarely travels to New York for the General Assembly.
The questions about the UN's role are hardly new, but have acquired fresh urgency as the organization struggles with deep financial problems, divisions among major powers and limited influence over conflicts from Ukraine to the Middle East.
Those concerns have gained new relevance since Trump's return to office last year. The US leader has pulled the US out of dozens of UN agencies and slashed Washington's budgetary contributions to the organization, pushing it to the brink of bankruptcy.
In his speech on Tuesday, Trump accused the UN of "imposing the far-left agenda of globalist bureaucrats who nobody ever elected."
UN facing deepening financial woes
The UN has a persistent budget shortfall, forcing it to cut the budget of its Secretariat by 9.2% for 2026. It laid off thousands of staff, sent peacekeepers home, and cut back on humanitarian and human rights work.
The United States, which has for years withheld much of its dues, is part of that problem.
The Trump administration last week paid $725 million for the regular budget, preserving its vote at the assembly, but still owes $1.3 billion to the regular budget and $2.9 billion for peacekeeping operations, the UN said.
The organization's problems extend beyond money, however.
Gridlock has long defined the UN Security Council, where five veto powers, including China, Russia and the US, rarely agree on anything substantive.
"There are two main challenges that the UN faces today: the first is its dire financial situation," said Eugene Chen, a former UN official.
"This is linked to a second, broader, challenge – the fact that member states no longer agree on what the form or function of the UN ought to be at a time of mounting global challenges," he said.
Outgoing Secretary-General Antonio Guterres launched a reform task force last year, known as UN80, which seeks to cut costs, remove duplication, move jobs to locations cheaper than New York and Geneva and improve efficiency.
It includes a 21% reduction in posts at the Secretariat and a review of more than 600 series of mandated Secretary-General's reports, aiming to reduce reporting by about 700,000 words in 2026.
Trump decries 'craven hypocrites' of UNHCR
Unlike in 2025, Trump did not use his Tuesday speech to complain about escalators or teleprompters and largely stuck to a script that focused on defending his record in the war with Iran and on the US economy.
Still, he inveighed against the "craven hypocrites" of the UN's Human Rights Council who "want America to open our borders to gangs and criminals from the world’s most dangerous places," and zeroed in on UNESCO, saying "these globalists are actively destroying the greatest cultures and most extraordinary heritage in history."
The UN has defended culture and education agency UNESCO's work as "unanimously acclaimed by major specialized organizations,” and the Human Rights Council as playing "a very important role in the promotion and protection of human rights worldwide."
Xi has sought to capitalize on Trump's often bellicose rhetoric by presenting China as a reliable partner on the global stage, especially for developing nations, and by using the UN as a platform to advance that message.
Over 1,000 meetings planned over UNGA week
For all the criticism of the UN, its annual meeting remains a forum for high-volume diplomacy. This week, member states planned more than 1,000 bilateral meetings, according to UN data.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines on Tuesday, the first such contacts since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed in July.
The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters the UN remained relevant, but she too criticized the organization for being "paralyzed when it comes to preventing or ending conflicts."
Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky used the venue to hold talks with Trump on ending the war with Russia, including a potential ceasefire on energy-related targets.
He was asked by a journalist whether years of meetings at the UN have brought any concrete results. He answered in English: "Today it helps us to meet. Maybe it's not too much, but it's something."

WATCH legendary Catholic TV bishop beatified
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:28:44 UTC
00:28:44 KST

WATCH legendary Catholic TV bishop beatified
Tens of thousands of Roman Catholics are gathering in Missouri for the beatification of Fulton John Sheen, the Bishop of Rochester, whose weekly TV show once rivaled Frank Sinatra’s in popularity.
Sheen, who died in 1979, will be beatified on Thursday afternoon in a ceremony at the Dome at America’s Center stadium in St. Louis. The beatification had been placed on hold for several years as the Catholic Church searched for a venue large enough to accommodate the 50,000 or so attendees expected.
Sheen’s beatification mass will be live streamed, starting at 2 PM St. Louis time (9 PM Central European Time)
Pope Leo XIV, who grew up just over 100 miles from Sheen’s first Diocese of Peoria, hailed the archbishop in an address at the Vatican on Wednesday. “May the example and intercession of this holy bishop, known for his evangelizing work through the media, inspire many others likewise to find new ways of spreading the gospel message with joyful enthusiasm,” the pontiff said.
Ordained a priest of the Diocese of Peoria in Illinois in 1919, Sheen became known as a keen theologian and philosopher. He was appointed auxiliary bishop for the Archdiocese of New York in 1951, Archbishop of Rochester in 1966, and the ceremonial Archbishop of Newport after his retirement in 1969.
Sheen’s influence, however, spread far beyond these dioceses. While a priest in Peoria, Sheen began hosting ‘The Catholic Hour’, a weekly radio show that drew roughly four million listeners by 1950. Two television shows – ‘Life is Worth Living’ and ‘The Fulton Sheen Program’ followed.
Fulton Sheen saw the dangers of 'false compassion' coming 50 years ago and called it out loud and clearpic.twitter.com/AQu57ILYIj
— Jack Posobiec (@JackPosobiec) September 6, 2026
‘Life is Worth Living’ aired at the same time as hit shows featuring Frank Sinatra and comedian Fulton Berle, and was widely expected to flop. However, it defied expectations, and when Sinatra’s show was canceled in 1952, Sheen’s program was the most popular of the three.
Sinatra and Berle had house bands, dancers, and lavish production budgets. However, with just a blackboard to illustrate his message, Sheen pulled in 30 million viewers per week at the height of his show’s popularity – a fifth of the US population at the time. Remarkably, it was estimated that 70% of his audience were Protestants, Jews, and non-believers.
'Our nation is too full with those who are crying 'down'.
Down with churches. Down with the police. Down with government. Can you build anything down? You cannot'
When Fulton Sheen went OFF on those seeking to destabilise society pic.twitter.com/iKbfJxqSrz
Although Sheen was a rigid believer in Catholic doctrine, he said that his show was “directed to Catholics, Protestants, Jews and all men of good will.” Sheen said that he would open with “something that was common to the audience and to me, I would gradually proceed from the known to the unknown or to the moral and Christian philosophy.”
Beatification is one step below canonization (the bestowing of sainthood) in Catholic law. As of the early 1980s, one miracle must be attributed to a person before they can be beatified. In 2019, Pope Francis formally recognized that a baby born without a heartbeat had been revived to perfect health after its parents prayed for Sheen’s intercession.

Xi seeks 'trust,' continued dialogue, 'healthy' competition as Trump hosts Chinese leader
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

00:25:03 KST

Saadet Gökce
24 September 2026•Update: 24 September 2026
Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for "trust," continued dialogue and "healthy competition" as US President Donald Trump hosted him at the White House.
Beijing and Washington should strengthen communication, Xi said, stressing that despite differences in their "national conditions," the two countries can better understand each other, seek common ground, and build mutual trust through "candid, in-depth, and continued dialogue."
He encouraged strengthened contacts between Chinese and US government departments, including those overseeing foreign affairs, the economy, financial cooperation, law enforcement, and people-to-people exchanges.
He also voiced support for greater exchanges between the two countries' legislative bodies.
"We should coexist in peace," Xi said, adding that as two major countries they "stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation."
Xi emphasized that China and the US do not need to avoid competition, but that it should be "healthy" and "kept within bounds." He called for "a race of catching up with each other," rather than a zero-sum "wrestling match in which one either wins or loses."
China and the US "must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation," he stressed, while calling for regular dialogue and improved mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention between their respective militaries.
"The Thucydides trap can be overcome," he said, referring to the risk of conflict between a rising power and an established one, a concept coming from US novelist Herman Wouk, referring to the ancient Greek historian.

U.S. intelligence warns Spain, France and Italy of possible Russian Gerbera drone attack from commercial ships, El Mundo reports

U.S. intelligence has warned several European governments that Russia is preparing a drone attack against Spain, France, or Italy, according to a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo. According to the outlet, the drones could be launched from a commercial vessel after being concealed inside a shipping container.
A source close to Lithuania’s Defense Ministry said:
“They will use drones launched from the sea, hidden in the container of a ship; it's not difficult at all.”
Lithuanian authorities even know the type of drone involved, according to the newspaper: the Gerbera, a Russian unmanned aircraft often used as a decoy or strike drone. The UAV weighs up to 18 kilograms, can reach speeds of about 160 kilometers per hour, and has a reported range of up to 600 kilometers. Its 4- to 5-kilogram warhead would not be powerful enough to destroy a major facility, but it could still start a fire or temporarily shut down a port or airport.
Lithuania received the information shortly after CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow on Aug. 25. According to El Mundo’s sources, authorities in Spain, France, and Italy were also warned about the possibility of such an operation, while a CIA report describing the potential attack in detail was circulated among European foreign ministries. The warning coincided with a response by French President Emmanuel Macron, who convened the country’s Defense Council on Sept. 16 and, two days later, invited leaders of all political parties to the Élysée Palace. After the meeting, the French president said protection of critical infrastructure against cyberattacks and drones would be strengthened due to “hybrid threats” from Russia.
El Mundo noted that elections are scheduled in all three countries in 2027 and that radical political forces could seek to capitalize on public fear about Russian attacks and general fatigue over the war in Ukraine. On Sept. 19, the pro-Russian Telegram channel Rybar published a map of possible targets in southern France, including aircraft plants, military bases, nuclear power stations, and petrochemical complexes that it said could be within range of Geran-5 drones launched from the northern coast of Algeria.
Last week, debris from a drone and a substance that investigators believe to be explosives were found in Lower Saxony near the German military’s Wunstorf Air Base. German federal prosecutors are examining whether the discovery is connected to an attempted act of sabotage at Leipzig/Halle Airport in early August that Berlin has blamed on Russia. In that incident, a drone fitted with a detonator was found there near a Ukrainian transport aircraft.

Mamdani also said Monday, reiterating a campaign promise, that he believed Netanyahu's International Criminal Court arrest warrant should be honored.
Mamdani's threat to arrest Netanyahu failed. His allies still see a victory | Analysis
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to address the UN General Assembly on Thursday, his first visit to New York after months of sabre-rattling with Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a conflict that neither man has shown any interest in ending.
Mamdani has had to back down from his promise to arrest Netanyahu when he lands in New York, but continues to call on federal authorities to do so. For his part, Netanyahu has made the mayor a target of his own attacks and a feature of his re-election campaign in Israel.

How Netanyahu, Israel's pariah premier, will gaslight the globe at the UN | Analysis
Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has always enjoyed his annual performance at the United Nations General Assembly. Over nearly two decades, he has enthusiastically grasped the opportunity to lecture and heckle world leaders in an address broadcast across the globe. His speeches, showcasing his command of English, are often peppered with props and gimmicks – from a cartoon Iranian nuclear bomb to the plans for the Auschwitz-Birkenau Nazi death camp.
But in the last few years, as the gloss of his well-tended image and Israel's broader stature has faded drastically, Netanyahu has found that despite the unmediated, one-directional set-up of the speech, he does not have full command of the immediate audience. They found a way to respond, with an equally arresting visual: walking out before or during his address. Last year, he spoke to a hall echoing with empty seats, interrupted only by the heckling of the families of Israeli hostages, then still held in Gaza by Hamas.
This year is likely to follow a similar pattern, intensified by the disintegration of support for Israel across much of the international community, not least among the American public, and the recent announcement of unprecedented sanctions on settlements by key Western allies. Undeterred, Netanyahu will be prepping his speech, shticks and soundbites for what has always been his core audience: the voters back home. And this year, more than ever before, his UN appearance will be carefully modulated to hit the most kneejerk, populist issues that could sway the October 27 elections his way.

Schism with rebel Catholic sect casts a pall over Pope Leo’s visit to France
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:18:23 UTC
00:18:23 KST

Schism with rebel Catholic sect casts a pall over Pope Leo’s visit to France
The Vatican’s recent excommunication of followers of a Catholic splinter sect, the Society of Saint Pius X, has revived a longstanding feud within the Roman Catholic Church ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s state visit to France. The ultra-conservative group has established an extensive network of schools and has attracted thousands of followers in France.
Nestled in the foothills of the Pyrénées, the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes is one of Catholicism’s most important pilgrimage sites, drawing millions of visitors each year, including sick and disabled believers hoping for a cure from its famed spring waters.
The hallowed site is also a flashpoint in a decades-long dispute dividing the Catholic world, which threatens to put a damper on Pope Leo’s visit to the shrine on Sunday – a highlight of the first papal state visit to France in almost 20 years.
Read morePope Leo XIV to trace back French ancestry, spiritual roots on visit to France
The dispute involving the ultra-conservative Society of Saint Pius X (SSPX) escalated sharply in July when the Vatican excommunicated followers of the splinter sect who defied Pope Leo by ordaining four bishops – including two Frenchmen – without his consent.
Following the schism, the bishop of Tarbes and Lourdes declared that SSPX members would be barred from organising events at the sanctuary in October for their annual Pilgrimage of Christ the King, which draws thousands of pilgrims from across Europe to the vast underground halls of the Basilica of Saint Pius X in Lourdes.
Challenge to the Vatican
Named after an early 20th-century pope who opposed modernising Catholic doctrine, the Society of Saint Pius X was founded in 1970 in response to the reforms of the Second Vatican Council (1962-1965, also known as Vatican II), which sought to reconcile the Roman Catholic Church with the modern world.
The Society notably rejects changes introduced at Vatican II to how Mass is celebrated, insisting that services be held in Latin and with priests facing the altar rather than the congregation. It also opposes religious freedom and interfaith dialogue.
SSPX members tend to espouse socially conservative views and are sometimes referred to as Lefebvrists, a reference to the organisation’s founder, Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre. They are thought to number roughly 600,000 worldwide, with the largest contingents in France and the US.
The Vatican and the rebel sect have long been at loggerheads. Pope John Paul II first excommunicated SSPX bishops in 1988, though his successor Benedict XVI reversed the decision two decades later in an attempt to bridge the divide. More recently, the late Pope Francis made further concessions on sacraments, allowing Society priests to celebrate marriages under certain conditions.
Those concessions have been rolled back as a result of the latest excommunications, which appear to go further than past censures of the sect.
In addition to targeting the Society’s six bishops, the Vatican’s July decree ruled that any lay members who “formally adhere” to the group “are to be considered schismatic and excommunicated”. The unusual move suggests Pope Leo intends to take a firmer stance than his predecessors.
“Leo XIV is a pacifist and a gentle man, determined to heal the wounds of the Church. But a key priority for him is the need for unity around the texts of Vatican II,” says Martin Dumont, a historian of Catholicism at Sorbonne University in Paris.
The pope had pleaded with the Society not to go ahead with the planned consecrations, warning that the “schismatic act” would constitute “a sin of extreme gravity”. By ignoring his warning, the sect effectively “challenged the authority of Leo XIV”, adds Dumont, for whom the bishops’ consecration “forced the Pope to take action”.
Glorifying Vichy France
With an estimated 700 priests worldwide, the ultra-conservative group remains a minority sect in the global Catholic Church – albeit a highly vocal one, backed by an extensive network of chapels, schools and religious communities. Its presence in France is growing year on year, says Dumont, “with large families ensuring it has the capacity to replenish its ranks”.
The SSPX has a historic bastion in the heart of Paris with the church of Saint-Nicolas-du-Chardonnet. It also has a strong foothold in western France, particularly in the historically pious regions of Brittany and Vendée, and runs a network of more than 50 schools labelled as “hors contrat”, meaning they do not follow the standard French curriculum.
Read moreFrom TikTok to church pews, France's Catholic influencers find a new flock
Critics, including former members of the Society, have accused it of entertaining cultish practices and sectarian abuse. According to a report in the Nouvel Obs weekly, the French Interior Ministry has placed the SSPX under surveillance.
French media investigations of SSPX-run schools have uncovered textbooks glorifying Marshal Philippe Pétain, the leader of Nazi-allied Vichy France. One history book made no mention of the term “Shoah”, commonly used in France to refer to the Holocaust.
When it comes to far-right leanings, the Society has a track record dating back to its founder, who “tended to express sympathy for authoritarian regimes”, notes Dumont.
One of the first bishops Lefebvre ordained in 1988, the Briton Richard Williamson, caused uproar by denying the Holocaust. He was eventually expelled over disagreements with SSPX leaders but went on to become a leading figure in the more radical Lefebvrist circles.
The Society made headlines again last year after one of its members attempted to celebrate a Mass in tribute to the Spanish dictator Francisco Franco and the founder of the fascist Falange movement, Antonio Primo de Rivera. The ordination ceremony that sparked the latest schism in July was attended by members of Italy’s neofascist Forza Nuova and a new far-right party, Italia Futura (Future Italy), which has emerged as a challenger to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Once close to Jean-Marie Le Pen’s far-right National Front party, the Society has since distanced itself from the rebranded National Rally of his daughter Marine Le Pen, largely due to the party’s shifting stance on abortion and same-sex marriage, Dumont says.
“While at one time members of the Society of Saint Pius X might have voted overwhelmingly for Jean-Marie Le Pen, nowadays sympathy for the National Rally is tempered by a certain indifference towards political parties, with many worshipers preferring to focus on prayer and pious works,” he says.
Appeasement
In the run-up to the pope’s visit, SSPX leaders in France have sought to strike a conciliatory tone, pledging not to seek a confrontation with the pope while also stressing that his stances on societal issues will be closely watched.
“Beyond the (Society’s) temporary difficulties (with the Vatican), this visit represents a special honour for all Catholics in France, and we cannot remain indifferent to it,” said Father Gonzague Peignot, one of the sect’s senior representatives in France.
“We are awaiting a statement from the Holy Father on the painful issue of euthanasia,” he added, referring to the recent approval by France’s National Assembly of a bill allowing adults with incurable illnesses to receive lethal medication – the culmination of years of debate over end-of-life care in France.
The Society is also hoping for firm condemnation of a 2024 vote by French lawmakers enshrining abortion rights in the French constitution.
Read morePope Leo to visit a secular France at odds with Catholic views on abortion, euthanasia
The splinter sect, which is appealing its excommunication, said it had written to the pope “to assure him that it did not receive these sanctions with bitterness or defiance”. It said its churches would mark his visit with moments of prayer, but no High Mass.
Other traditionalist groups will feature prominently during the papal visit, including the High Mass celebrated on Place de la Concorde and the Champs-Elysées in Paris on Saturday, where they will have their own designated area, Dumont says.
One group with far-right leanings, SOS Calvaires, has already played a conspicuous role, building a four-metre-high cross that will stand behind the Pope on Friday evening as he holds a prayer vigil with 80,000 youths at the Stade de France.

China gets F-35 parts containing sensitive US technology – Bloomberg
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:18:17 UTC
00:18:17 KST

China gets F-35 parts containing sensitive US technology – Bloomberg
China has obtained potentially sensitive components from the F-35, the US military’s most advanced stealth fighter jet, after the parts were unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong while being shipped from Australia to the US, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people briefed on the incident.
The incident first reported by Politico last week occurred earlier this year, when a shipment of allegedly unserviceable F-35 parts from Australia that was bound for the US was inexplicably rerouted.
US shipping giant UPS was transporting an F-35 canopy and weapons-bay door from the Australian Air Force to the US for inspection and possible repair or disposal, people familiar with the incident told Bloomberg. The two components, manufactured by Lockheed Martin, were coated with radar-absorbing material designed to enhance the aircraft’s stealth capabilities, according to two sources cited by the outlet.
One of the sources said the transport aircraft stopped in South Korea on its way to the US, after which the shipment was rerouted to Hong Kong. It remains unclear why the aircraft stopped there, why the shipment was sent to Hong Kong, or whether the rerouting was intentional or accidental, the source said. Two sources added that Chinese authorities subsequently seized the components, which have not been returned.
The F-35, one of the world’s most advanced fighter jets, is operated by around 20 countries, including South Korea, Japan, Singapore and Australia. Australia serves as a regional hub in the Indo-Pacific for storing spare parts and maintaining F-35s operated by nearby US allies.
At least two congressional committees are investigating the latest incident, the news agency noted. Earlier this week, Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles confirmed that Canberra was working with the US and Lockheed Martin to examine its role in the shipment blunder. Marles stressed that the missing components were not sensitive.
According to a Lockheed Martin spokesperson in Australia, “the components in question are unserviceable and deemed low risk for exploitation.”
The disclosure of the incident comes at a politically sensitive time for the two countries, as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington on Wednesday for a state visit with his US counterpart, Donald Trump.
China’s Foreign Ministry said it was not aware of the incident, while the Hong Kong government declined to comment on specific cases.

Cancer-linked ‘forever chemical’ found in blood of residents near UK factory
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:17:52 UTC
00:17:52 KST

Burak Bir
24 September 2026•Update: 24 September 2026
Elevated levels of a cancer-linked “forever chemical” have been found in blood samples from dozens of residents living near a factory in the UK, a law firm said Thursday.
Blood tests on residents of Thornton Cleveleys living near a large chemical factory revealed increased levels of PFOA, a type of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS), Leigh Day said in a statement.
The results showed that of the 49 residents tested, nearly 70% had elevated PFOA levels, placing them at higher risk of health problems associated with the chemical, including high cholesterol and some cancers.
PFOA is part of the PFAS group of chemicals, known as “forever chemicals” because they resist breaking down in the environment and can accumulate in human tissue.
The statement said the participants live near an industrial site operated by AGC Chemicals, where PFOA was historically used until 2012.
“The site was previously operated by ICI until 1992. It is estimated around 178 tonnes of PFOA has been released by the site since the 1950s,” it noted.
Wyre Council, in conjunction with the Environment Agency (EA), has carried out soil testing in the area, with samples from residents’ properties and nearby allotments showing elevated levels of PFOA, the firm said.
Leigh Day has also been investigating PFAS contamination in the area, working with experts led by Dave Megson at Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU).
The blood testing was carried out during the summer of 2026 by an expert team from MMU, with the results relayed to participants on Sept. 23.
“The results showed levels of PFOA above 20 nanograms per millilitre (ng/ml) in 69.4% of participants, placing them in the high-risk category, with the overall average at 26 ng/ml.”
The statement said the findings were comparable to those recorded among residents in Ohio living near a DuPont factory in the case adapted into the film Dark Waters, where an average level of 32.9 ng/ml was recorded.
“The results of our testing project in Thornton Cleveleys are hugely concerning,” said Sarah Moore, a Leigh Day partner who leads the firm’s investigations.
She added: “The available evidence suggests that PFAS exposure can lead to serious health impacts, including cancers, when it reaches elevated levels.”

airBaltic had accumulated EUR 503 million in debt and EUR 856 million in lease obligations on date it filed for Chapter 11obligations  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:13:31 UTC
00:13:31 KST

RIGA - On the date the restructuring process, or Chapter 11, was filed, September 14, Latvia’s national airline airBaltic had total liabilities of EUR 503.3 million, while operating lease obligations totaled EUR 855.6 million, according to a declaration submitted to the court by airBaltic Chief Financial Officer Vitolds Jakovlevs.
The funded debt consisted of approximately EUR 398.2 million in liabilities related to 14.5 percent secured bonds maturing in 2029. Of this amount, the principal of the bonds was EUR 393.8 million, while accrued and unpaid interest totaled approximately EUR 4.4 million.
Another approximately EUR 7.9 million consisted of a loan from BluOr Bank, secured by airBaltic cargo hangar located at Riga Airport, and the land use rights associated with its construction; the debt also includes the remaining balance of a loan from the Latvian government in the amount of approximately EUR 18.6 million.
The airline also had approximately EUR 78.6 million in finance lease obligations for eight aircraft, seven engines, and a flight simulator. According to an assessment by Seabury, the financial advisor engaged by airBaltic, repurchasing these assets through DIP or Debtor-in-Possession financing, could "unlock" approximately EUR 170 million in equity value in the aircraft and engines.
Meanwhile, operating lease obligations for 46 aircraft and seven engines totaled EUR 855.6 million.
In his statement, Jakovlevs noted that, according to the business plan, airBaltic’s fleet is expected to be reduced from 54 to 36 aircraft by the end of this year, by returning approximately 20 surplus aircraft, reducing leasing costs, and achieving annual cost savings of approximately EUR 45 million.
At the same time, on the date the Chapter 11 petition was filed, airBaltic’s cash balance was EUR 1.13 million, according to a court filing by Stephan Krastev, vice president of the financial consulting firm Seabury Global Aviation Advisors.
His affidavit states that approximately EUR 350 million in new financing is needed to implement airBaltic’s restructuring process. Without immediate access to financing, the airline would be unable to maintain its day-to-day operations, would be forced to suspend flights, and would ultimately face liquidation, Krastev emphasized.
He cited the consequences of the Covid-19 pandemic, the impact of Russia’s war in Ukraine, the shortage of Pratt & Whitney engines and aircraft downtime, as well as rising fuel prices linked to the conflict in Iran as the main reasons for financial difficulties.
In the summer of 2026, airBaltic and its advisors approached bondholders, restructuring funds, and other potential lenders. Offers were received from four potential financiers, but none of them provided sufficient funding or acceptable terms to meet the company’s needs.
He added that a group of bondholders also offered financing, but it came with very strict conditions, a very high price, priority over all other creditors, and operational requirements that could disrupt flight operations. In Krastev’s assessment, the offer was too expensive, did not allow enough time for restructuring, and did not provide sufficient benefits to save the company.
He emphasized that a broad outreach to investors began in mid-August. The fund Strategic Value Partners (SVP) was particularly significant. Ten potential investors signed confidentiality agreements and conducted a financial review of the company. Investors were provided with information on the company’s financial position, fleet, business plan, cash flow, and restructuring strategy. As a result, several proposals were received.
Krastev emphasized that nearly all potential lenders put forth three requirements - first, to repay aircraft lease obligations; second, to grant first-priority security interests; and third, to secure future financing even before the next loan tranche is disbursed.
He concluded that the company evaluated several financing options, but in his assessment, the SVP fund’s offer specifically provides the necessary liquidity, allows more time to implement the restructuring, and enables the company to take advantage of the benefits of Chapter 11 process to maintain the company’s operations.
As reported, airBaltic has begun restructuring its financial obligations in accordance with the Chapter 11 procedure set forth in U.S. law.
In total, airBaltic has received a binding commitment from lenders to provide up to EUR 350 million in new financing (DIP) to ensure the company’s liquidity and operations during the Chapter 11 process.
To date, airBaltic has received the first tranche of financing in the amount of EUR 140 million, of which EUR 78.925 million will be used to repurchase eight aircraft and seven engines.
The financing was arranged by SVP, and Barclays, Hayfin Capital Management, Morgan Stanley, Oaktree Capital Management, and Strategic Value Partners have committed to providing it. The interest rate is SOFR +8 percent, or approximately 12 percent at present, but this process will also involve additional commission fees totaling up to EUR 52.5 million.
Consequently, the previous plan to raise up to EUR 257 million at an annual interest rate of 25 percent from bondholders will not be implemented. Meanwhile, the bondholder group Ad Hoc Group, which owns a portion of the 14.5 percent secured bonds issued by airBaltic, maturing in 2029, has filed objections in court regarding the manner in which DIP financing is being provided and how bondholders’ rights are being curtailed.
Chapter 11 protection shields airBaltic from creditor claims until the restructuring of its liabilities is completed.
The company also reports that flights and customer service will continue as usual. All flights will operate according to the scheduled flight plan; existing tickets and reservations remain valid, and passengers can continue to purchase tickets and travel with airBaltic as before.
Upon completion of this process, the final outcome will be a so-called reorganization plan, which must be approved by the court. The process is expected to be completed by mid-2027.
It was also reported that airBaltic bondholders supported the capitalization of the next two interest payments on the bonds in August, as well as several other measures that provide the airline with additional flexibility in implementing its revised business plan.
Bondholders supported the capitalization of interest payments due on August 14 and November 14 of this year, adding them to the principal amount of the bonds rather than paying them in cash. A decision was also made to grant a temporary exemption from minimum liquidity requirements through November 2026.
The airBaltic group’s revenue last year increased by 4.2 percent compared to 2024, totaling EUR 779.344 million. Meanwhile, airBaltic group’s losses last year totaled EUR 44.337 million, which is 2.7 times less than in 2024. The airline carried a total of 5.2 million passengers in 2025, which is 1 percent more than in 2024.
Last summer, Germany’s national airline, Lufthansa, became a shareholder in airBaltic. Currently, the Latvian government owns 88.37 percent of airBaltic’s shares, Lufthansa holds 10 percent, the company Aircraft Leasing 1, owned by Danish businessman Lars Thuesen, a financial investor, holds 1.62 percent, and 0.01 percent is held by other shareholders. The company’s share capital is EUR 41.819 million.

Saeima cuts excise tax rate on diesel fuel and gasoline  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:13:29 UTC
00:13:29 KST

RIGA - On Thursday, Saeima adopted amendments to the Law on Limiting Price Increases for Petroleum Products, which provide for an even greater reduction in the excise tax rate on diesel fuel, as well as a reduction in the excise tax rate on gasoline.
The amendments will take effect on October 1, 2026.
The adopted changes provide for a 16.7 percent reduction in the excise tax rate applicable to diesel fuel used as transportation fuel, bringing it down to the minimum tax level set by the European Union.
Consequently, the excise tax on diesel fuel will be reduced from EUR 396 per 1,000 liters to EUR 330 per 1,000 liters.
Meanwhile, the excise tax rate on unleaded gasoline has been reduced by 11.7 percent, setting it at EUR 490 per 1,000 liters. Until now, the excise tax on gasoline had not been reduced.
Economics Minister Viktors Valainis (Greens/Farmers) noted that changes in the excise tax are reflected at gas stations with a time lag, and the impact on prices is only partially passed on.
Valainis emphasized that achieving an immediate impact on prices would require either an even steeper reduction in the excise tax or a cut in the value-added tax (VAT) rate.
The retail price of diesel is expected to drop by EUR 0.08 if fuel retailers fully pass on the tax reduction to the fuel price.
The changes also call for a reduction in the excise tax rate on unleaded gasoline, setting it at EUR 490 per 1,000 liters, to be in effect until December 31, 2026. The reduction in the excise tax rate will amount to EUR 0.065 per liter, or nearly EUR 0.08 per liter when VAT is included. Consequently, the retail price of gasoline is expected to decrease by approximately EUR 0.08, provided that fuel retailers pass on the full amount of the tax reduction to the fuel price.
The explanatory memorandum states that by reducing the excise tax rate on fuel for three months - from October 1, 2026, to December 31, 2026 - is projected to have a negative impact on state budget revenue amounting to EUR 14.4 million.
Taking into account the procedures for declaring and paying excise tax and VAT, as well as the related crediting of revenues to the state budget, the measure’s impact on the state budget’s cash flow is projected to be minus EUR 9.6 million in 2026 and minus EUR 4.8 million in 2027.
To offset the negative impact of the statutory provisions on state budget revenues in 2026, a one-time compensatory measure is planned to utilize the revenue surplus from the sale of confiscated criminally obtained assets, since the actual collection of these revenues in 2026 will exceed the amount originally planned for that year.

From 17 September to 17 December 2026, BODIES Evolution, one of the world’s best-known educational exhibitions dedicated to the human body, is on display at Teika Plaza (Brīvības gatve 201, Riga). Over the years, the exhibition has been presented in numerous countries and has attracted more than 30 million visitors, becoming one of the largest international exhibition projects dedicated to anatomy and science outreach.
The exhibition offers visitors a journey inside the human body, revealing what is normally hidden from view.
“BODIES Evolution features eight complete plastinated human bodies, as well as a wide range of anatomical specimens that allow visitors to explore the abdominal cavity, reproductive system, heart, skull and muscles in greater detail,” says exhibition producer Gabriel Rios (Portugal). “The exhibition provides a valuable opportunity to learn about the human body and how it functions in an accessible and engaging way. Another important idea behind the exhibition is to help visitors understand how fragile the human body is and recognise the importance of taking care of our health from an early age.”
Scientific accuracy, an accessible approach and a contemporary exhibition format have made BODIES Evolution one of the most recognised international exhibition projects dedicated to the human body. In an interview with The Insider, Fedotov confirmed that he is Stepanenko’s father. LETA has previously reported on his generous donations to the politician, who, in turn, refused to explain their origin. The newspaper 41+ Solnechnogorsk (41+ Солнечногорск) reported in November 2022 that Forma ZHBI, together with KROST, had begun producing so-called "dragon’s teeth". In a December 6 publication, Fedotov himself confirmed his willingness to continue providing assistance: "If additional help is needed to produce a new batch, we are always ready to participate." He noted that the company is capable of producing more than 150 concrete structures per day.
Fedotov also explained his company’s role in the production of stoves - partners prepared the blueprints, while his company supplied the metal and assembled the stoves. In Moscow, they were additionally equipped with grates and chimneys. "The products are then sent to the front," said Fedotov.
The same article reported that 2,000 defensive fortifications and approximately 50 stoves were produced over the course of a month. The concrete barriers were sent to the Belgorod region and the Russian-occupied territories of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
In an October 2024 publication, Alexei Shashkin, a representative of the Valor (Доблесть) foundation, named Fedotov among the businesspeople helping to prepare shipments for delivery to the war zone. The newspaper reported that Fedotov had donated a GAZ Sobol vehicle worth one million rubles to the foundation. Russian combat units, including BARS, have also received shipments from the foundation.
The family’s former company, Forma-Stroy - in which Fedotov held a 60 percent stake and Stepanenko’s half-sister, Anna Makarovskaya, held a 10 percent stake - also received military contracts. The STAR database contains a 2015 contract for the delivery of sand to a military unit worth RUB 48,000. Meanwhile, in 2016-2017, the company signed three contracts with the NIID Engine Research Institute worth approximately RUB 3.27 million, including reconstruction work on a diesel engine production facility. One contract, worth approximately RUB 1.76 million, involved adapting the facility for the serial production of diesel engines. The Moscow Region Construction Expertise Register lists funding for the project from the Russian federal budget.
NIID was added to the European Union (EU)’s sanctions list on May 20, 2025, as a supplier to the Russian Ministry of Defense that supports the military-industrial complex. Forma-Stroy entered into these contracts before the sanctions were imposed. In 2019, Forma-Stroy acquired the company Forma ZHBI.
In total, Checko lists seven Forma-Stroy contracts with public clients worth approximately RUB 6.5 million. Official records from 2015 and 2016 also confirm subsidies totaling RUB 4.88 million for the purchase and leasing of equipment.
Fedotov’s Forma complex was also visited by Viktor Bout, an illegal arms dealer nicknamed "Merchant of Death," who was sentenced in the U.S. to 25 years in prison and was extradited to Russia in 2022 as part of a prisoner exchange program. In a report published on August 2 of this year, the television channel 360 covered a meeting between him and State Duma Deputy Valery Seleznyov with the complex’s employees. The representative of Russia’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) thanked Fedotov for the tour of the complex. The party’s report also mentioned honoring the families of military personnel involved in the war.

Millions of people, one planet: World Cleanup Day 2026 moves from cleaning up to changing habits  - The Baltic Times
Unknown

Presidents, ministers, celebrities and millions of volunteers in more than 192 countries answered the call to "Strive for Five".
On 20 September 2026, the ninth global World Cleanup Day again turned one day into a worldwide wave of action. Preliminary data show millions of participants in more than 192 countries and territories.
From Tallinn to the United Nations stage
This year's global UN observance took place in Shaoxing, China, co-hosted by UN-Habitat. Let's Do It World President Heidi Solba took part in the inauguration, representing the movement that began when 50,000 Estonians cleaned their country in five hours in 2008. The President of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, is patron of World Cleanup Day 2026.
"It is important to understand that World Cleanup Day is a powerful platform for cooperation," said Heidi Solba, Co- founder, President of Let's Do It World and Head of the Global Network. "It connects governments and civil society, building a safe and trusted foundation for creating solutions, for inclusion, for empowerment and for resolving crises. We believe our network is exactly that strong muscle, able to mobilise on a massive scale. We call on all governments to cooperate and support that action”.
Last and this year's message calls for engaging at least 5% of the world's population, the critical mass at which caring for the environment becomes a social norm.
"We cannot keep cleaning up the world while producing and consuming more and more," said Siiri Tiivits-Puttonen, CEO of Let's Do It World. "Cleanup is important, but the next step is to look at what and why we consume, how long we use things and how we can prevent waste before there is anything to clean up."
Global Leaders who rolled up their sleeves
In Namibia President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah marked World Cleanup Day by relaunching the national Cleanup Namibia Campaign. In Estonia Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna cleaned Tallinn's Linnahall area with the diplomatic corps, while Estonian embassies around the world joined the day in their host countries. In Zimbabwe the national commemoration in Harare took place under the patronage of First Lady Dr AuxilliaMnangagwa, linking clean communities to the country's tourism future. In Jordan The Ministry of Environment led cleanups in ten governorates, bringing together government agencies, security services, municipalities, schools and volunteers.
Throughout the EU, the EU made World Cleanup Day its flagship date, with EU Delegations joining cleanups from Buenos Aires to the Ecuadorian Amazon. In Senegal, the EU Delegation, the City of Dakar and the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Organising Committee cleaned all 19 municipalities of Dakar, ahead of the first Olympic event ever hosted in Africa, leader of Let’s Do It Senegal Stephan Senghor said “This historic World Cleanup Day united Senegal to tackle waste, planting the seed for a permanent ecological legacy that will outlast Dakar 2026”.
In Germany, World Cleanup Day was spearheaded by Let's Do It Germany together with its partners, with Bonn serving as the event's hub. The day kicked off with an inclusive football match, welcomed by Bonn Mayor Guido Déus, who served as patron of the Bonn event, alongside Viktor Haase, State Secretary at North Rhine-Westphalia's Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Transport, and Let's Do It Germany President Holger Holland.
This year Brazil engaged more than one million students were reached with the message "Be the 5% Who Will Change the World” with Instituto Limpa Brazil, the Let’s Do It World network organization. Edilainne Muniz Pereira, Executive Director of Instituto Limpa Brasil – Let’s Do It!: “When more than one million students are invited to look at the places where they live and realize that they have the power to transform them, we are doing much more than organizing a cleanup — we are helping shape a new generation of leaders”.
The uninhabited North Sea island of Mellum just 27 volunteers collected around 15 cubic meters of rubbish washed ashore, demonstrating that the waste has no borders and have reached to the most abounded areas.
Stars on the ground - In Namibia, some of the country's best-known entertainers, including Gazza, Lize Ehlers and Adriano Visagie, joined a Celebrity Clean-Up in Windhoek. In Oman, World Cleanup Day was led by Fahad Al Abri, an environmental activist, singer and Guinness World Record holder whose song "The Earth Is Entrusted to Us" has inspired young Omanis to clean their beaches.
The day was connected through three hubs: the Global Broadcast in Riga, the Global Call Center in Tallinn and the Global Media Center in Kyiv.
Final 2026 results will be published once national teams have verified their data.
The next World Cleanup Day will take place on 20 September 2027.
About World Cleanup Day
The movement started to born in Estonia in 2008, when 50,000 people cleaned the entire country in just five hours. It grew into Let's Do It World, a civic network whose national teams in more than 190 countries and territories lead the day on the ground. The first global World Cleanup Day took place in 2018. In December 2023, the UN General Assembly unanimously adopted Resolution 78/122, initiated by Estonia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Climate and Let's Do It World, proclaiming 20 September as World Cleanup Day. Since 2024 it has been part of the official UN calendar, giving governments worldwide a clear mandate to act alongside their citizens. Between 2018 and the end of 2025, 139 million people from 211 countries and territories took part, collecting more than 870,000 tonnes of waste.
The World Cleanup Day 2026 Global Broadcast was hosted in Riga with financial support from the Latvian Environmental Protection Fund.

Verston Group company Smartecon to build one of the Baltics’ largest battery storage facilities in Estonia  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:13:14 UTC
00:13:14 KST

Smartecon has signed a contract to build the Raudsepa battery energy storage system (BESS), one of the largest in the Nordic and Baltic region by power and storage capacity. The engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract for the facility in Tsirguliina, southern Estonia, covers design, equipment supply, construction, commissioning and grid code compliance. The scope also includes building a 330 kV substation.
Raudsepa will have a power capacity of 192 MW and an energy storage capacity of 420 MWh. The project is backed by Taaleri Energia’s SolarWind III Fund and co-investors. Construction will begin in September 2026, with the facility expected to be fully operational by November 2027.
According to Magno Kure, Smartecon’s CEO, delivering Raudsepa requires extensive expertise in both energy systems and infrastructure construction. “We are responsible for delivering the entire facility, from design through to commissioning. The engineering challenge lies in integrating the battery storage equipment, control systems and 330 kV substation into a fully functioning system that meets grid code requirements. We manage equipment supply, construction and commissioning as one integrated process,” said Kure.
Battery storage is an essential part of today’s energy system. It helps balance electricity generation and consumption throughout the day, stabilise electricity prices and support the system at critical times. Raudsepa’s 420 MWh storage capacity is equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of about 150 households, assuming 2,800 kWh per household per year.
According to Jüri Tamm, co-CEO of Verston Group, Europe’s infrastructure must be planned with transport and energy systems in mind. “Reliable connections and a secure energy supply underpin Europe’s economy and security. Alongside energy generation, we need grids and storage facilities that deliver electricity to consumers when it is needed. We commend the client’s decision to procure Raudsepa as a turnkey project, entrusting a single partner with responsibility from design through to commissioning. At Verston, we combine infrastructure construction and energy expertise to deliver projects of this kind,” said Tamm.
The project is jointly owned by Taaleri Energia’s SolarWind III Fund, a co-investor in the fund, and KJK Fund III, managed by KJK Capital. Evecon and French independent power producer Corsica Sole developed it. The facility will use LG Energy Solution’s battery storage equipment and European-made inverters from Power Electronics.
Smartecon OÜ is an energy infrastructure company founded in 2012 that designs, builds and maintains energy generation and storage solutions. Over 14 years, the company has built more than 1,000 solar power plants across five countries. In 2025, Smartecon reported revenue of nearly EUR 35 million and a net profit of EUR 0.3 million. Smartecon is part of Verston Group.
Verston is an infrastructure construction and maintenance group founded in Estonia and expanding internationally, with activities spanning roads, railways, energy and urban infrastructure. Established in 2010, the company combines engineering expertise, digital working methods and responsible resource use to build durable infrastructure and maintain it throughout its lifecycle. Alongside its operations in Estonia, Verston is expanding into other European markets, including Poland.

Unknown Publisher

00:13:03 KST

The Klaipėda Port Authority is taking an important step forward in the development of the southern part of the port by launching a tender for construction works. The selected contractor will be responsible for creating 100 hectares of new land in an area that is currently part of the Curonian Lagoon, as well as carrying out other major infrastructure works.
“Contractors who will build the breakwaters are already on site, and we are now taking another major step towards turning this ambitious idea into reality by launching the construction tender for the entire area. This is an important milestone that brings us closer to goals that go far beyond simply building new quays. The development of the southern part of the port will create new opportunities for both the Port of Klaipėda and Lithuania. The new area will attract investors and enable the development of new terminals, bringing new jobs, economic growth and an even stronger transport and logistics sector,” says Algis Latakas, Director General of the Klaipėda State Seaport Authority.
The contractor will be responsible for creating the new land area in the Curonian Lagoon and building a 1,300-metre quay. The works will also include removing a section of the 110 kV Marios–Juodkrantė overhead power line and installing a new underground power cable, carrying out part of the construction work on one of the breakwaters, dredging the port waters, installing stormwater drainage systems, and building a shoreline protection wall near Kiaulės Nugara Island.
The southern port development project will significantly expand the current port area. New terminals will be developed in the 100-hectare area, container handling capacity will be expanded, and the area also offers potential for the marine engineering industry. Once fully developed, the southern part of the port is expected to have the capacity to handle around 30 million tonnes of cargo per year.
The project, which will significantly increase the port’s operating and cargo handling capacity, accounts for the largest share of the investment programme under the Port of Klaipėda’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan, with nearly EUR 600 million allocated to its implementation. Including future private investment, the total value of the development is expected to exceed EUR 1 billion.
Earlier this month, during a Government meeting held at the Klaipėda Port Authority, the procedure for leasing the new area, or parts of it, through a competitive tender was approved. An international tender to select an operator for the future site will be launched later this year.

During a Latvian business delegation’s visit to Germany, technology company dots. and autonomous mobility company HOLON agreed to cooperate in advancing the autonomous transport sector in the Baltics. The partners plan to secure EUR 30 million in funding from various European Union funds and development programmes. The initiative includes establishing an autonomous vehicle manufacturing facility in Latvia and implementing pilot projects for passenger transport in urban and regional areas.
“Autonomous transport is becoming one of the most important areas in the future development of mobility. It is therefore essential for Europe to build its own technological, manufacturing and infrastructure capacity. By working with international partners, Latvia has an opportunity to become a significant strategic player in this sector. One of the key prerequisites is the establishment of an autonomous vehicle manufacturing facility in Latvia, which would provide a foundation for technology development, testing and deployment. It would facilitate the implementation of various pilot projects in cities and regions, help address current passenger transport challenges, and create new business and export opportunities. This would enable Latvia to become not only a user of autonomous mobility solutions but also a centre for their development, manufacturing and export across the Baltic and European markets,” says Edgars Starķis, Head of Traffic Safety Innovation and Smart Mobility Solutions Development at technology company dots.
One of the central areas of cooperation being considered by the two companies is the establishment of an autonomous vehicle manufacturing facility in Latvia. It would lay the foundation for a comprehensive industry ecosystem in the Baltics and the wider Baltic Sea region, encompassing vehicle and component manufacturing, software and artificial intelligence development, testing, certification, infrastructure adaptation and vehicle maintenance. Local manufacturing would also create new high-value-added jobs and facilitate the integration of Latvian companies into European autonomous mobility supply chains.
The second area of cooperation involves autonomous transport pilot projects in cities and regions. These projects would test the use of autonomous mobility solutions in everyday passenger transport, including connections to public transport hubs, improved accessibility in less densely populated areas and routes where conventional transport services are difficult or economically inefficient to operate. The pilot projects would make it possible to assess the safety of the technology, infrastructure readiness, public demand and the regulatory changes required for the sector.
In the near future, the partners will develop a joint funding strategy, refine the development model for the manufacturing facility and define the technical requirements for potential pilot projects. Public- and private-sector partners, municipalities, transport operators, research institutions, and local technology and manufacturing companies are expected to be involved in preparing the projects. Their implementation will depend on the conditions of the relevant funding programmes, agreements between the partners and the receipt of the necessary permits.
The companies reached the agreement on future cooperation during a business delegation’s visit to Germany organised by the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia and attended by Latvia’s Minister of Economics, Viktors Valainis. During the discussions, dots. and HOLON identified common areas for development and agreed to work together on securing European Union funding, establishing a manufacturing project and implementing autonomous transport pilot projects in the Baltic States.
Latvian information technology company dots. develops data- and artificial intelligence-based solutions. Its smart traffic solutions team, Fits Traffic, specialises in traffic data analysis, infrastructure management, mobility planning and road safety solutions.
German company HOLON develops fully electric autonomous shuttles for public transport and mobility services. Cooperation with dots. would combine HOLON’s expertise in autonomous vehicle development with Latvia’s technological capabilities in traffic data analysis, smart mobility solutions and transport infrastructure management.

====================================================================================================

Critical infrastructure is becoming a tool for exerting geopolitical pressure - expert  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:12:47 UTC
00:12:47 KST

RIGA - Critical infrastructure is becoming a tool of geopolitical pressure, said Luca Tagliaretti, executive director of the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre, on Thursday at the CyberShield cybersecurity and technology forum.
He noted that, given the current geopolitical situation, it is important to take the developments affecting critical infrastructure seriously. Looking at Ukraine and the data, it is evident that 80 to 85 percent of cyberattacks are directed against civilian infrastructure - the energy sector, transportation, telecommunications, and public services.
The situation in Europe is not quite as dramatic, but a significant number of attacks are also being observed. More often than not, these are directed against government agencies, transportation, digital services, and financial services. According to Tagliaretti, these are fundamental elements of society, which is why they require special attention.
Tagliaretti noted that critical infrastructure is no longer merely a system that ensures the functioning of society, but is also becoming an instrument of geopolitical pressure. Therefore, it is essential to ensure its protection against threats that are no longer merely civilian in nature, but also relate to the defense sector.
He explained that the European Union's first step was to establish a level playing field and a common understanding of cybersecurity. This is ensured by two regulations that establish a common level of security in critical sectors and reinforce the understanding that cybersecurity is no longer merely a technical issue.
According to Tagliaretti, cybersecurity is an issue that must also be addressed at the company board level, by establishing the responsibility of board members and directors for system security. This helps establish a common terminology and policy framework. Furthermore, through the so-called omnibus approach, this framework is extended to various pieces of legislation, ensuring a unified regulatory approach.
The second key piece of legislation is the Cybersecurity Act. Tagliaretti emphasized that, for the first time, this Act extends responsibility not only to companies that must protect their own technology and servers, but also to companies that offer technologies and products on the European market. In his view, this will raise the level of protection and help ensure that protection extends beyond the borders of the European Union.
Speaking about the role of the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre in implementing this legislation, Tagliaretti noted that several funding mechanisms have been established to help the industry prepare for the requirements of the Network and Information Security Directive (NIS2) and the Cybersecurity Act.
One example is the Secure project, which focuses on the Cybersecurity Act. Several member states are participating in it, but companies outside these countries can also apply. Companies can use this opportunity to test their software and adopt best practices from other companies in the sector.
In addition to providing funding, the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre, together with the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), has developed technologies and systems to protect critical infrastructure, particularly in connection with the Cybersecurity Solidarity Act. Tagliaretti emphasized that when assessing risks and threats to various critical infrastructure sites, it is important to recognize that cyberattacks do not stop at borders.
Dmitrijs Nikitins, Chief Technology Officer at Latvian technology company Tet, noted at the forum that cyberattacks are becoming increasingly automated, so defense systems must be able to operate in a similar manner.
He explained that, unlike a human attacker, an artificial intelligence model can operate continuously and, following a failed attempt, use the information gathered to adapt its actions in the future. Nikitins also noted that many criminal organizations are attempting to adapt artificial intelligence models to exploit vulnerabilities.
At the same time, he noted that these tools are not yet fully automated, but development is moving in that direction. As companies increasingly adopt artificial intelligence, the potential attack surface is growing.
Nikitins pointed out that AI agents with extensive access privileges and MCP servers capable of performing various autonomous actions are already being used. If an attacker manages to gain control of such an agent, the consequences could be serious.
He explained that attackers can exploit devices that have not been updated for a long time on the network, automatically scanning the network, checking for various CVE vulnerabilities, finding an attack vector, and gaining initial access. Afterward, artificial intelligence agents can analyze the situation, find other agents with access to internal systems, and pass on the information and access rights they have obtained. As a result, a human may be involved only in the final stage of the attack, while the scale and speed of the attack increase significantly.
Nikitins pointed out that the cyber defense process currently involves many activities - network scanning, vulnerability identification and assessment, task creation, troubleshooting, and applying patches, all of which take time. On the attackers' side, however, these processes can occur continuously and automatically.
Therefore, in his view, the approach to cybersecurity must change, and the level of automation must be increased. Defense must operate continuously while maintaining human oversight.
Nikitins noted that results from 2025 show that the average time required to transfer gained access to another group decreased from eight hours to 22 seconds. This means that once one group gains access, it can be transferred almost immediately to other groups for further action.
He noted that tools are available on the market that can automate the detection, assessment, and remediation of vulnerabilities, but their use requires human oversight.
Based on data from Tet, Nikitins noted that an increase in the number of automated attacks has been observed on the network. This year, the number of automated denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks has increased by 30 percent, and there has also been a rise in the number of carpet bombing and large-scale DDoS attacks. According to him, this underscores the need to invest in cybersecurity and protect both the operator's and the customers' infrastructure.
Email data also shows an increase in the number of spam and malicious emails. Currently, 62 percent of all emails reaching a company's email gateway contain spam, phishing attempts, or malicious code. Similarly, the number of targeted phishing attacks-which are created using artificial intelligence-is on the rise.
Nikitins pointed out that artificial intelligence can sometimes know more about people and their data than even their closest relatives do, so organizations must be prepared for such attacks.
He also mentioned a sixfold increase in emergency patching incidents over the past year and a half. The risk of vulnerabilities being exploited has become so high that it is necessary to stop other work and install patches immediately. Whereas a company previously had only a couple of such incidents, there are now more than a dozen.
As previously reported, the CyberShield cybersecurity and technology forum is taking place in Riga on Thursday. The forum's program focuses on cybersecurity policy and resilience, the impact of artificial intelligence on security, as well as real-world cyberattacks and organizations' ability to respond to them in a timely manner.

EBRD raises economic growth forecast for Latvia and Estonia, but keep's Lithuania's forecast unchanged  - The Baltic Times
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-24
15:12:40 UTC
00:12:40 KST

RIGA - The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has raised its gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecasts for Latvia and Estonia, but has kept its economic growth forecast for Lithuania unchanged.
The EBRD’s latest projections indicate that Latvia’s GDP will grow by 2.4 percent this year, rather than the 2 percent estimated in June.
Compared to the June forecasts, the EBRD’s projections for Estonia’s economic development have also improved. While it was previously estimated that Estonia’s economy would grow by 2.1 percent this year, the EBRD’s latest projections now expect it to grow by 2.4 percent.
Meanwhile, the EBRD forecasts 3 percent growth for the Lithuanian economy this year, unchanged from its June projection.
The EBRD notes that Latvia’s economic growth has accelerated from 2.1 percent last year to 2.8 percent in the first six months of this year, thanks to a rise in investment, but the rise in imports has outpaced the growth in exports. The bank forecasts that Latvia’s budget deficit will rise from 2.5 percent of GDP last year to 4.2 percent next year and 5.4 percent in 2028, taking into account increased defense spending.
At the same time, the EBRD expects Latvia’s GDP to grow by 2.1 percent next year, rather than the 2.3 percent previously forecast. The bank, however, has kept its economic growth forecasts for Lithuania and Estonia unchanged at 2.2 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
The EBRD has lowered its economic growth forecast for the countries in its region by 0.6 percentage points to 2.5 percent for this year, while a 4 percent increase is expected in 2027.
The bank has lowered its economic growth forecast for Ukraine this year by 0.7 percentage points to 1.5 percent, while next year’s forecast has been reduced by 1.5 percentage points, with a 0.7 percent contraction expected.
The EBRD is jointly owned by 64 member states, the European Union (EU), and the European Investment Bank (EIB). European countries play a dominant role in the bank, though several other countries, including the United States and Japan, also participate in decision-making. It was founded in 1991 to help the former Soviet bloc countries in Europe and Central Asia transition to a market economy. The bank operates in 29 countries.

The leaders’ visit got off to a positive start, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announcing within minutes of Xi’s arrival that the US and China agreed to extend their trade truce by around two months to Jan 10.
Struck in 2025r, that deal has kept down tariffs after Trump set off a trade war with China during the first months of his second term.
Some members of Trump’s own party have criticised the manner in which he’s hosting Xi, including Senator Roger Wicker, typically a reliable ally of the president who chairs the chamber’s Armed Services Committee.
“I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome,” Wicker said this week.
“His guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.”
While the two leaders projected warmth, tensions have also mounted behind the scenes.
Shortly before Xi landed, Bloomberg News reported the Chinese government has taken possession of F-35 stealth aircraft parts that were diverted to Hong Kong while being sent to the US from Australia.
Trump has acknowledged the two countries’ rivalry even as he seeks to court Xi.
Trump has said he favours unabated AI development in order for the US to outpace China, despite industry leaders’ concerns the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.
The US president rejected such warnings as a “hoax.”
It’s unclear how deeply the two leaders plan to delve into the trickier parts of the US-China relationship.
Trump told reporters on Sept 23 they would discuss the war in Iran “and many other subjects, but it’s all coming along well.” BLOOMBERG
